entries.title: C0048: exact critical magnetization target
entries.statement: CONJECTURE; CURRENT OPENNESS UNKNOWN. For every integer q>=3,d>=3, the zero-field nearest-neighbor unit-coupling Potts model on Z^d is conjectured to satisfy m(beta_c)>0, where its weight is exp(beta sum 1{equal neighboring spins}), m(beta)=(q mu^1_beta(sigma_0=1)-1)/(q-1), and beta_c=inf{beta:m(beta)>0}. Equivalently theta^w(p_c,q)>0 for ordinary FK open connectivity and p=1-exp(-beta). The 2017 primary Conjecture 2 and the 2026-09-07 ranking are dated evidence, not a current openness certificate.

entries.title: FK: sharp conditional product bound for disjoint edge sets
entries.statement: DRAFT AUTHOR PROOF; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING; NO NOVELTY CLAIM. For a finite FK measure with arbitrary boundary partition, 0<p<1 and q>=1, and disjoint nonempty edge sets C_i, P(each C_i contains an open edge)<=product_i(1-(1-p)^|C_i|). This is sharp for the cut-event intersection at q=1. It passes to infinite-volume limits for finite cylinder events; separating cuts with sum_i(1-p)^|C_i|=infinity rule out an infinite ordinary open cluster at the separated vertex.
assumptions: for the infinite-cluster corollary, every infinite ordinary path meets every C_i
locally finite infinite graph for the infinite-cluster corollary

entries.title: Finite-width FK strips: no finite-temperature Potts order
entries.statement: DRAFT AUTHOR PROOF; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING; NO NOVELTY CLAIM. If H is finite connected with m vertices and G=Z Cartesian-product H, then for every q>=1 and p<1, ordinary connectivity across n layers is at most [1-(1-p)^m]^n, uniformly over finite-volume boundary partitions. The root-to-end-layer probability in a centered interval is at most twice this bound. Free and wired FK infinite-volume limits have no infinite ordinary open cluster for p<1. For integer q>=2 the monochromatic Potts magnetization is zero at every finite delta-convention beta, so beta_c=infinity.
assumptions: ordinary paths use graph edges and not auxiliary wiring identifications
q>=1 for FK; integer q>=2 for Potts
homogeneous unit ferromagnetic couplings and zero field

entries.title: Six-regular amenable strip obstructs a degree-only ordering bridge
entries.statement: DRAFT AUTHOR PROOF; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING; NO NOVELTY CLAIM. The graph Z Cartesian-product K5 is connected, simple, vertex transitive, amenable and six-regular, but its q=3 zero-field ferromagnetic Potts model has beta_c=infinity. Thus q>=3 plus six-regularity, transitivity and amenability alone do not imply finite-temperature order or a finite-temperature first-order transition.
assumptions: the hypothetical bridge has no Z^3 geometry, growth-dimension or p_c<1 hypothesis
all couplings are homogeneous and equal to 1

entries.title: Exact q=3 ladder witness against marginal-product upper bounds
entries.statement: DRAFT AUTHOR PROOF; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING; NO NOVELTY CLAIM. On the free FK width-two three-layer ladder with q=3,p=1/2, let A and B mean that the two respective longitudinal two-edge cuts contain an open edge. P(A)=P(B)=409/925, P(A intersection B)=181/925, and P(A intersection B)-P(A)P(B)=144/855625>0. The disjoint cuts are dependent, so multiplying their marginal probabilities does not give an upper bound.
assumptions: six vertices and seven edges listed in check_cutsets.py
cut crossing means nonempty cut, not actual point connectivity

entries.title: Integer Potts states do not determine a real-q phase threshold
entries.statement: DRAFT AUTHOR PROOF; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING; NO NOVELTY CLAIM. If q_c is a threshold over real cluster weights, discontinuity for every integer q>=3 together with continuity at q=2 does not logically imply q_c=2. The monotone predicate D(q) iff q>5/2 satisfies these integer assertions while its real threshold is 5/2. The intake parenthetical equivalence needs this quantifier distinction and a definition of q_c.
assumptions: q_c is interpreted over real q
this is a logical countermodel, not a random-cluster model
source-context correction remains conditional until reviewed

relations.rationale: From "H is finite connected with m vertices" and to "disjoint nonempty edge sets C_i": the m longitudinal edges in each layer boundary form such disjoint cuts, giving the strip bound.
From "Z Cartesian-product K5" and to "H is finite connected with m vertices": taking H=K5 gives zero finite-temperature magnetization on the six-regular graph.
From "The disjoint cuts are dependent" and to "P(each C_i contains an open edge)<=product_i(1-(1-p)^|C_i|)": the witness explains the conditional chain required by the upper bound.
From "threshold over real cluster weights" and to "For every integer q>=3,d>=3": the latter quantifier does not settle the former threshold.
